subproblem.title: Affine approximation lemma (Simon 5.2.5, corrected)
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l and p > n there is C = C(n,l,p) > 0 such that: if U is open, V has generalized mean curvature H in U, 0 < delta <= 1/4 and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho hold (rho > 0, theta >= 1 mu_V-a.e., 0 in spt V, B_rho(0) in U, omega_n^-1 rho^-n mu_V(B_rho(0)) <= 1 + delta, (rho^(p-n) integral_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p)^(1/p) <= delta), then for every xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0) and sigma in (0, 2 delta rho] there is an n-dimensional subspace T with C^-1 (sigma^-n integral_{B_{sigma/2}(xi)} |p_{T_xM} - p_T|^2 dmu_V)^(1/2) <= sigma^-1 h + (sigma^(p-n) integral_{B_sigma(xi)} |H|^p)^(1/p) and sigma^-1 h <= C delta^(1/(2n+2)), where h = sup{dist(x - xi, T) : x in spt V cap B_sigma(xi)} (all in [0,inf]).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 5, 2.3, 2.4 and the printed proof of Lemma 2.5 (pp. 108-110), with the documented erratum (the mean-curvature term added to the first inequality of (double dagger)) and these corrections: (a) monotonicity is used with the constant of Ch. 4, 4.2 read correctly, kappa = (p-n)/(4p), i.e. Lambda = 4 p delta/(p-n); since Lambda need not be small for delta <= 1/4 when p is close to n, the pinched bounds 2.4 are only used for delta <= delta_P(n,p), and a separate mass bound valid for ALL delta in (0,1/4] (step 1a, from the general error estimate of 4.5) is proved before the large-delta case is treated; (b) the printed route 'first inequality from Remark 2.2' needs p >= 2, so the first inequality is derived from Lemma A (the L^1 form of the computation proving 2.1), valid for every p > n; (c) the bounds of 2.4 are used at centres in B_{3 delta rho}(0).

Notation (contract). mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (M = V.carrier, theta = V.mult); spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu; p_x := V.tangentProj x and p_x^perp := I - p_x; |A| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm), ||A|| the operator norm, ||A|| <= |A| <= sqrt(rank A) ||A||; B_s(y) is the closed ball and B^o_s(y) the open ball; omega_n := unitBallVolume n; K(z,s) := (s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) in [0,infinity] (the contract's scaledLpNorm); E(z,s,T) := s^-n integral_{B_s(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu (tiltExcess); kappa := (p-n)/(4p) > 0; a := 1/(2n+2). Under 2.3, if B_s(z) is contained in B_rho(0) then K(z,s)^p = s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p <= (s/rho)^(p-n) rho^(p-n) integral_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p, so K(z,s) <= (s/rho)^(1-n/p) delta <= delta.

Facts used:
(F1) [Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7, Rem. 1.8, Thm. 1.9; contract tangentProj] For mu-a.e. x the approximate tangent space T_xM of M with respect to theta exists; at such x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto the n-dimensional space T_xM, and Theta^n(mu,x) = theta(x) (Rem. 1.8(2)). The map x -> p_x is mu-measurable and bounded (|p_x - p_T|^2 <= 4n), so tilt integrals over compact subsets of U are finite: by Ch. 3, Rem. 1.3 and Rem. 1.8(1), M is covered up to an H^n-null set by countably many H^n-measurable pieces M_j contained in embedded C^1 submanifolds N_j, and for H^n-a.e. x in M_j the space T_xM exists and equals T_xN_j, which depends continuously on x in N_j; since T_xM is unique where theta(x) > 0 (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), p_x agrees mu-a.e. with a Borel map. If Gamma is the graph of a Lipschitz map over (a subset of) an n-plane, then T_xM = T_x Gamma for H^n-a.e. x in M cap Gamma (Rem. 1.8(1)), and T_x Gamma is the range of the differential of the graph map at H^n-a.e. x in Gamma (Rademacher, Ch. 2, 1.4).
(F2) mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0 and mu(R^(n+l) minus U) = 0, so mu-a.e. point lies in spt V; mu(K) < infinity for compact K in U; H^n(M minus spt V) = 0 (because mu(M minus spt V) = 0 and theta > 0 on M); spt V is relatively closed in U; if y in U minus spt V then mu(B^o_r(y)) = 0 for some r > 0.
(M) [Monotonicity: Simon Ch. 4, 4.1-4.10, with the coefficient in front of Lambda in 4.2 equal to kappa = (p-n)/(4p), the value required by the integration after 4.4 (cf. SimonGMT Chapter04 `lpMeanCurvatureKappa`, `LpAnnularCorrection`)]. Let y in R^(n+l) and R > 0 with B_R(y) in U and K(y,R) <= kappa Lambda for some Lambda > 0. (Under 2.3, whenever B_R(y) is contained in B_rho(0) we have K(y,R) <= delta, so Lambda := delta/kappa = 4 p delta/(p-n) is admissible; Lambda <= 1 as soon as delta <= kappa.) Then there are F : (0,R) -> (0,infinity) and numbers G(s,r) such that for all 0 < s <= r < R:
 (M.i) e^-Lambda <= F(r) <= e^Lambda and |F(r) - 1| <= (1/2) e^(Lambda/2) Lambda (r/R)^(1-n/p); if Lambda <= 1, then |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda (r/R)^(1-n/p) <= Lambda; F(r) -> 1 as r -> 0.
 (M.ii) Phi(r) - Phi(s) = G(s,r) integral_{B_r(y) minus B_s(y)} |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 |x - y|^(-n-2) dmu(x), where Phi(t) := F(t) t^-n mu(B_t(y)) + F(t) - 1 and G(s,r) in [e^-Lambda, e^Lambda].
 (M.iii) Hence Phi is nondecreasing, Theta(y) := lim_{s -> 0} omega_n^-1 s^-n mu(B_s(y)) exists, and omega_n Theta(y) = lim_{s -> 0} Phi(s) <= Phi(r) for every r in (0,R); in particular mu({y}) = 0.
 (M.iv) [Ch. 4, 4.9 and 4.10(1), applied to V restricted to an open set W in U on which H is in L^p_loc] If theta >= 1 mu-a.e. and W is an open subset of U each point of which is the centre of a ball as above, then Theta >= 1 at every point of spt V cap W: Theta = theta >= 1 mu-a.e. by (F1), Theta is upper semicontinuous on W (4.9), so {x in W : Theta(x) < 1} is open and mu-null, hence disjoint from spt mu. Under 2.3 this applies to W = B^o_rho(0) (H is in L^p(B_rho(0)) since K(0,rho) <= delta < infinity).
 (M.v) If Lambda <= 1 and 0 < s <= r < R, then s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= e^(2 Lambda) r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda. [By (M.ii) Phi(s) <= Phi(r), so F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) = Phi(s) - (F(s) - 1) <= F(r) r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + (F(r) - 1) + Lambda <= e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 Lambda; divide by F(s) >= e^-Lambda.]
(P) [2.4 of the text, with explicit constants]. Assume 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho) with delta <= min{1/8, kappa}, so Lambda := delta/kappa <= 1. Consider the smooth functions of t in [0, min{1/8, kappa}] (with Lambda_t := t/kappa)
 g_+(t) := e^(2 Lambda_t) (1 + t)(1 - 3t)^-n + 2 e^(Lambda_t) Lambda_t/omega_n,
 g_-(t) := e^(-Lambda_t) (1 - Lambda_t/omega_n),
 g_c(t) := e^(Lambda_t) (e^(Lambda_t) (1 + t)(1 - 3t)^-n - 1) + e^(Lambda_t) Lambda_t/omega_n.
Since g_+(0) = g_-(0) = 1 and g_c(0) = 0, there is C_P = C_P(n,p) >= 1 with g_+(t) <= 1 + C_P t, g_-(t) >= 1 - C_P t and g_c(t) <= C_P t on that interval. Put delta_P := min{1/8, kappa, 1/(2 C_P)}.
Claim. If delta <= delta_P, |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2, then (P.i) mu(B_s(y)) <= (1 + C_P delta) omega_n s^n <= 2 omega_n s^n and Theta(y) <= 1 + C_P delta; if moreover y in spt V, then (P.ii) mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - C_P delta) omega_n s^n >= omega_n s^n/2 and (P.iii) integral_{B_s(y)} |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 |x - y|^(-n-2) dmu(x) <= C_P omega_n delta (integrand := 0 at x = y).
Proof. R_y := (1 - 3 delta) rho >= 5 rho/8 > rho/2 >= s, B_{R_y}(y) is contained in B_rho(0) (as |y| + R_y <= rho), so (M) applies at y with R = R_y and Lambda = delta/kappa <= 1, and mu(B_r(y)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n for r < R_y. (P.i): for s <= r < R_y, (M.ii),(M.i) give F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) = Phi(s) - (F(s) - 1) <= Phi(r) + Lambda <= e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 Lambda; dividing by F(s) >= e^-Lambda and letting r -> R_y, omega_n^-1 s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= g_+(delta); Theta(y) is the limit as s -> 0. (P.ii): Theta(y) >= 1 by (M.iv), so by (M.iii) F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n - (F(s) - 1) >= omega_n - Lambda and s^-n mu(B_s(y)) >= e^-Lambda (omega_n - Lambda) = omega_n g_-(delta) (here omega_n - Lambda > 0 because g_-(delta) >= 1/2). (P.iii): for 0 < t < s <= r < R_y, (M.ii),(M.iii) give integral_{B_s(y) minus B_t(y)} |p_x^perp(x-y)|^2 |x-y|^(-n-2) dmu <= e^Lambda (Phi(r) - Phi(t)) <= e^Lambda (e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + Lambda - omega_n Theta(y)) <= e^Lambda (e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + Lambda - omega_n); let r -> R_y and t -> 0 (monotone convergence, mu({y}) = 0) to get <= omega_n g_c(delta).
Lemma A (L^1 form of the computation proving Lemma 2.1; valid for every V with generalized mean curvature H in U, no p needed). Let z in R^(n+l), r > 0 with B_r(z) contained in U, T an n-dimensional subspace and h >= 0 such that dist(x - z, T) <= h for every x in spt V cap B_r(z). Then
 integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 r^-2 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu.
Proof. Fix phi in C^infinity(R,[0,1]) with phi = 1 on (-infinity,1/2], phi = 0 on [1,infinity), |phi'| <= 3; put zeta(x) := phi(|x - z|/r) (smooth, since phi is constant near 0), x' := p_{T^perp}(x - z) (so |x'| = dist(x - z, T)) and X := zeta^2 x'. X is C^infinity, has compact support and tsupport X is contained in B_r(z), a subset of U, so X is admissible in the definition of generalized mean curvature, and X . H is mu-integrable because H is in L^1_loc(mu) on U. Since DX(x)v = zeta^2 p_{T^perp} v + 2 zeta (grad zeta . v) x', at every x where p_x is a rank-n orthogonal projection (mu-a.e. by (F1)) div_M X = trace(DX o p_x) = zeta^2 trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) + 2 zeta grad zeta . p_x x' = zeta^2 s + 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x', where s := (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2 (for rank-n orthogonal projections trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) = n - trace(p_T p_x) = (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2) and p_T x' = 0. All integrands are bounded and measurable with support in B_r(z), which has finite measure (F2). The first variation identity gives integral zeta^2 s dmu = - integral 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' dmu - integral zeta^2 x' . H dmu. As |(p_x - p_T) x'| <= ||p_x - p_T|| |x'| <= sqrt(2s) |x'| and 2 sqrt(2s) zeta |grad zeta| |x'| <= (1/2) zeta^2 s + 4 |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2, we get integral zeta^2 s dmu <= 8 integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 dmu + 2 integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu. Finally zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), 0 <= zeta <= 1, |grad zeta| <= 3/r, zeta = 0 off B_r(z), and |x'| <= h for mu-a.e. x in B_r(z) (such x lie in spt V by (F2)); hence (1/2) integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 72 r^-2 integral_{B_r(z)} |x'|^2 dmu + 2 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu.

Proof. Fix n >= 1, l and p > n; alpha := a = 1/(2n+2). Let 0 < delta <= 1/4, let 2.3 hold, xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0), sigma in (0, 2 delta rho].

1. Mass bounds.
(1a) [all delta in (0,1/4]] Put Lambda_1 := p/(p-n) and C_0 := e^(2 Lambda_1) ((4/3)^n (5/4) + e^(Lambda_1/2) Lambda_1/omega_n). If |y| <= rho/4 and 0 < s <= rho/2 then mu(B_s(y)) <= C_0 omega_n s^n.
Proof: R := 3 rho/4; B_R(y) is contained in B_rho(0), so K(y,R) <= delta and (M) applies at y with Lambda = delta/kappa <= (1/4)/kappa = Lambda_1. For s <= r < R, (M.ii) and the GENERAL error bound of (M.i) give F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) = Phi(s) - (F(s) - 1) <= Phi(r) + |F(s) - 1| <= e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + |F(r) - 1| + |F(s) - 1| <= e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_rho(0)) + e^(Lambda/2) Lambda. Let r -> R, use mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n <= (5/4) omega_n rho^n and F(s) >= e^-Lambda: s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= e^Lambda (e^Lambda (4/3)^n (5/4) omega_n + e^(Lambda/2) Lambda) <= C_0 omega_n.
(1b) [delta <= delta_P] The claim (P) above holds.

2. First inequality, for EVERY n-dimensional subspace T. Let T be an n-plane and h := sup{dist(x - xi, T) : x in spt V cap B_sigma(xi)}; the set contains xi, and 0 <= h <= sigma, so heightSup = ofReal h. B_sigma(xi) is contained in B_{3 delta rho}(0), a subset of B_rho(0) and of U, so K := K(xi, sigma) <= delta is finite. Lemma A with z = xi, r = sigma:
 integral_{B_{sigma/2}(xi)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 sigma^-2 h^2 mu(B_sigma(xi)) + 4 h integral_{B_sigma(xi)} |H| dmu.
By (1a) (|xi| <= rho/4, sigma <= rho/2), mu(B_sigma(xi)) <= C_0 omega_n sigma^n, and by Hoelder integral_{B_sigma(xi)} |H| dmu <= (integral_{B_sigma(xi)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) mu(B_sigma(xi))^(1-1/p) <= K sigma^(n/p - 1) (C_0 omega_n sigma^n)^(1-1/p) = (C_0 omega_n)^(1-1/p) K sigma^(n-1). Hence
 sigma^-n integral_{B_{sigma/2}(xi)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 C_0 omega_n (h/sigma)^2 + 4 (C_0 omega_n)^(1-1/p) (h/sigma) K <= C_2 (h/sigma + K)^2,
with C_2 := max{144 C_0 omega_n, 2 (C_0 omega_n)^(1-1/p)}. Taking square roots, C_2^(-1/2) (sigma^-n integral_{B_{sigma/2}(xi)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu)^(1/2) <= sigma^-1 h + K. Since ofReal(sigma^-1) * heightSup = ofReal(h/sigma) and scaledLpNorm = ofReal K, this is the first inequality of the lemma for every constant C >= C_2^(1/2) and every n-plane T.

3. Second inequality when delta_P < delta <= 1/4. For every n-plane T and x in B_sigma(xi), dist(x - xi, T) <= |x - xi| <= sigma, so sigma^-1 h <= 1 <= delta_P^(-alpha) delta^alpha. Take T := horizontalPlane n l (spanned by the orthonormal vectors e_1, ..., e_n, hence n-dimensional). With C >= max{C_2^(1/2), delta_P^(-alpha)} both inequalities hold (the first by step 2).

From now on delta <= delta_P (book's proof). Every point used below lies in B_{3 delta rho}(0) and every radius is <= 4 delta rho <= rho/2, so (P) applies.

4. Conical excess (book (1)). Let y in spt V cap B_sigma(xi); then |y| <= |xi| + sigma <= 3 delta rho, and |x - y| <= 2 sigma on B_{2 sigma}(y), so by (P.iii)
 integral_{B_{2 sigma}(y)} |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 dmu <= (2 sigma)^(n+2) integral_{B_{2 sigma}(y)} |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 |x - y|^(-n-2) dmu <= (2 sigma)^(n+2) C_P omega_n delta. (1)

5. Covering by small balls (book (2),(3)). Put A := delta^alpha in (0,1). If y_1, ..., y_N in spt V cap B_sigma(xi) have pairwise disjoint balls B_{A sigma/2}(y_j), then N <= C_4 A^-n with C_4 := 4^(n+1): each such ball has measure >= omega_n (A sigma/2)^n/2 by (P.ii), and they are disjoint subsets of B_{2 sigma}(xi), whose measure is <= 2 omega_n (2 sigma)^n by (P.i). Choose such a family of maximal cardinality (N >= 1 since {xi} is admissible). By maximality every y in spt V cap B_sigma(xi) has B_{A sigma/2}(y) meeting some B_{A sigma/2}(y_j), i.e. |y - y_j| <= A sigma; so
 spt V cap B_sigma(xi) is contained in the union of the B_{A sigma}(y_j), and N <= C_4 delta^(-alpha n). (2),(3)

6. Choice of a good tangent plane (book (4)-(6)). Let f(x) := sum_{j=1}^N |p_x^perp(x - y_j)|^2 (mu-measurable by (F1), nonnegative). Since B_sigma(xi) is contained in B_{2 sigma}(y_j) for every j, summing (1) gives integral_{B_sigma(xi)} f dmu <= N (2 sigma)^(n+2) C_P omega_n delta <= C_5 delta^(1 - alpha n) sigma^(n+2), C_5 := C_4 2^(n+2) C_P omega_n. Let lambda := 4 C_5 delta^(1 - alpha n) sigma^2/(omega_n A^n) = (4 C_5/omega_n) delta^(1 - 2 alpha n) sigma^2. By Chebyshev, mu({x in B_sigma(xi) : f(x) > lambda}) <= C_5 delta^(1 - alpha n) sigma^(n+2)/lambda = omega_n A^n sigma^n/4, while mu(B_{A sigma}(xi)) >= omega_n (A sigma)^n/2 by (P.ii). Hence {x in B_{A sigma}(xi) : f(x) <= lambda} has positive measure, and by (F1),(F2) it contains a point x_0 in spt V at which T_{x_0}M exists. Put T := T_{x_0}M (n-dimensional; p_{x_0} = p_T). Then for every j, |p_{T^perp}(x_0 - y_j)| <= lambda^(1/2) = (4 C_5/omega_n)^(1/2) delta^(1/2 - alpha n) sigma = C_6 delta^alpha sigma, because 1/2 - alpha n = 1/(2n+2) = alpha (the book's choice of alpha). Since |x_0 - xi| <= A sigma = delta^alpha sigma, |p_{T^perp}(y_j - xi)| <= (C_6 + 1) delta^alpha sigma for all j.

7. Height bound. For x in spt V cap B_sigma(xi) choose j with |x - y_j| <= A sigma (step 5); then dist(x - xi, T) = |p_{T^perp}(x - xi)| <= |p_{T^perp}(y_j - xi)| + |x - y_j| <= (C_6 + 2) delta^alpha sigma. Hence sigma^-1 h(xi, sigma, T) <= C_7 delta^alpha, C_7 := C_6 + 2, i.e. ofReal(sigma^-1) * heightSup(xi, sigma, T) <= ofReal(C_7 delta^(1/(2n+2))).

8. Conclusion. C := max{C_2^(1/2), C_7, delta_P^(-alpha), 1} > 0 depends only on n, l, p. For delta <= delta_P the plane of steps 6-7 satisfies the second inequality, for delta > delta_P the plane of step 3 does, and every n-plane satisfies the first inequality (step 2, as C^-1 <= C_2^(-1/2)).

subproblem.title: Conical approximation theorem (Simon 5.6.1)
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l and Lambda > 0 there is C = C(n,l,Lambda) such that: if lambda, theta, delta in (0,1/4), |xi| = 1 - theta, U is open with closed B_1(0) in U, V has generalized mean curvature H in U (mu = mu_V), |mu(B_1(0))/omega_n - mu(B_lambda(0))/(omega_n lambda^n)| + r^(1-n) integral_{B_r(0)} |H| dmu <= delta for every r in [lambda, 1], and mu(B_1(0)) <= Lambda, then for all rho in (0, theta] and tau in [2 lambda, 1]: mu(B_{(1 - delta^(1/4)) rho}(xi)) <= tau^-n mu(B_{tau rho}(tau xi)) + C delta^(1/4) |log lambda| and tau^-n mu(B_{tau rho}(tau xi)) <= mu(B_{(1 + delta^(1/4)) rho}(xi)) + C delta^(1/4) |log lambda|.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 5, Theorem 6.1 and its printed proof (p. 124-127), steps (1)-(12). Repairs: the trivial case delta^(1/4)|log lambda| > 1 is separated (this gives the mass bounds needed for the Cauchy-Schwarz step (7)); the piecewise-linear cutoff gamma is replaced by C^1 cutoffs and a limit; the homogeneous functions h = h_t are constructed explicitly with |Dh(x)| <= 2/(delta^(1/4) rho |x|); in the printed (1) the integrand is r^-n |D^perp r|^2 = r^(-n-2) |x^perp|^2; tau = 1 is trivial and every tau in [2 lambda, 1) is allowed (printed 'tau in [lambda, 1/2]' is a typo). Notation: mu = V.weight, r = |x|, x^perp := p_{T_x^perp} x, grad^M r = p_x(x/r) with |grad^M r|^2 = 1 - r^-2 |x^perp|^2 (mu-a.e.), integral_{dB_t} g := integral_{M cap dB_t} g theta dH^(n-1); balls closed; |log lambda| >= log 4 > 1. No lower bound on theta is used.

Facts used: (F1),(F2) (tangent planes a.e., measurability, local finiteness); (3.18) [Ch. 4, 3.18]: if tau^(1-n) integral_{B_tau(0)} |H| dmu <= delta for sigma <= tau <= rho' (B_{rho'}(0) in U), then |(rho'^-n mu(B_{rho'}) - sigma^-n mu(B_sigma)) - integral_{B_{rho'} minus B_sigma} r^-n |D^perp r|^2 dmu| <= delta log(rho'/sigma); (4.11) [Ch. 4, 4.11] layer-cake for integrals of r^(1-n)|H| and r^-n; (CoA) [Ch. 3, 2.9] coarea for r on the countably n-rectifiable M: integral_A g |grad^M r| theta dH^n = integral_0^infinity integral_{M cap A cap dB_t} g theta dH^(n-1) dt for nonnegative measurable g.

Proof. C denotes constants depending on n, l, Lambda.
0. Trivial case. If delta^(1/4)|log lambda| > 1: B_{(1-delta^(1/4))rho}(xi) is in B_1(0), so the left side of the first inequality is <= Lambda < Lambda delta^(1/4)|log lambda|; and B_{tau rho}(tau xi) is in B_tau(0), so by (3.18) tau^-n mu(B_{tau rho}(tau xi)) <= mu(B_1) + delta |log lambda| <= (Lambda + 1) delta^(1/4)|log lambda|. So both inequalities hold if C >= Lambda + 1. Henceforth delta^(1/4)|log lambda| <= 1, hence delta |log lambda| <= 1.
1. By (3.18) with sigma = lambda, rho' = 1 and the hypothesis: integral_{B_1 minus B_lambda} r^(-n-2) |x^perp|^2 dmu <= C delta |log lambda| (1); and tau^-n mu(B_tau) <= mu(B_1) + delta |log lambda| <= Lambda + 1 for tau in [lambda, 1] (2). With (4.11): integral_{B_1 minus B_lambda} r^(1-n) |H| dmu <= C delta |log lambda| (3) (write r^(1-n) = 1 + (n-1) integral_r^1 t^-n dt and use t^(1-n) integral_{B_t} |H| <= delta), and integral_{B_1 minus B_lambda} r^-n dmu <= C (Lambda + 1) |log lambda| (by (2)).
2. First variation identity (book (5)). Let h in C^1(R^(n+l) minus {0}; [0,1]) be homogeneous of degree 0 with |Dh(x)| <= k/|x|. Since x . Dh(x) = 0: |x . p_x(Dh)| = |x^perp . Dh| <= k |x^perp|/r (4). For psi in C^1_c((0,1]) put X := h r^-n psi(r) x (in C^1_c(U), support in B_1(0)); mu-a.e. div_M X = n psi h r^(-n-2)|x^perp|^2 + psi'(r) h r^(1-n) |grad^M r|^2 + psi r^-n x . grad^M h. Insert into the definition of generalized mean curvature, let psi increase to the indicator of [s,t] (lambda <= s < t <= 1) with psi' concentrating at s and -t, and use (CoA) with g = h r^(1-n)|grad^M r|: for a.e. such s, t, with A(s) := integral_{dB_s} h r^(1-n) |grad^M r|,
 A(s) - A(t) + n integral_{B_t minus B_s} h r^(-n-2) |x^perp|^2 dmu = - integral_{B_t minus B_s} r^-n (h x . H + x . grad^M h) dmu.
 By (3), (4): |A(s) - A(t) + n integral_{B_t minus B_s} h r^(-n-2)|x^perp|^2| <= C delta|log lambda| + k integral_{B_1 minus B_lambda} r^(-n-1) |x^perp| dmu.   (5)
3. Homogeneity (book (6),(7)). Take s = tau t with tau in [2 lambda, 1) and t >= 1/2 (then s >= lambda). Multiply by t^(n-1) <= 1 and use h(tau x) = h(x); by Cauchy-Schwarz, (1) and step 1:
 | tau^(1-n) integral_{dB_{tau t}} h |grad^M r| - integral_{dB_t} h |grad^M r| | <= C delta |log lambda| + C k (Lambda+1)^(1/2) delta^(1/2) |log lambda|.   (7)
4. Choice of h (book (8)). For rho in (0, theta], |xi| = 1 - theta, t in (|xi| - rho, |xi| + rho) (so t >= 1 - 2 theta >= 1/2), let phi in C^infinity(R; [0,1]) with phi = 1 on (-inf, (1 - delta^(1/4)) rho], phi = 0 on [rho, inf), |phi'| <= 2/(delta^(1/4) rho), and h_t(x) := phi(|t x/|x| - xi|). Then h_t = 1 on dB_t cap B_{(1-delta^(1/4))rho}(xi), h_t = 0 on dB_t minus B_rho(xi), on dB_{tau t} the set {h_t > 0} lies in B_{tau rho}(tau xi), and |Dh_t(x)| <= 2/(delta^(1/4) rho |x|), i.e. k = 2 delta^(-1/4) rho^-1. (7) gives for a.e. such t:
 integral_{dB_t cap B_{(1-delta^(1/4))rho}(xi)} |grad^M r| <= tau^(1-n) integral_{dB_{tau t} cap B_{tau rho}(tau xi)} |grad^M r| + C rho^-1 (Lambda+1)^(1/2) delta^(1/4) |log lambda| + C delta |log lambda|.   (8)
(Rigour of the pointwise-in-t statements: since h_t depends on t, keep psi_eps with psi_eps' = 1/eps on [tau t - eps, tau t] and -1/eps on [t, t + eps], write the identity of step 2 for (h_t, psi_eps), integrate it over t in (|xi| - rho, |xi| + rho) first (all integrands are jointly measurable and integrable), and let eps -> 0 only at the end; by (CoA) the averaged boundary terms converge for these integrated quantities.)
5. Integrate (8) over t in (|xi| - rho, |xi| + rho) and use (CoA) twice (the substitution t' = tau t turns the first right-hand term into tau^-n integral_{B_{tau rho}(tau xi)} |grad^M r|^2 dmu; B_{(1-delta^(1/4))rho}(xi) lies in the shell |xi| - rho < r < |xi| + rho):
 integral_{B_{(1-delta^(1/4))rho}(xi)} |grad^M r|^2 dmu <= tau^-n integral_{B_{tau rho}(tau xi)} |grad^M r|^2 dmu + C delta^(1/4) |log lambda|.   (9)
 Since |grad^M r|^2 = 1 - r^-2 |x^perp|^2 and r <= 1, (1) gives mu(B_{(1-delta^(1/4))rho}(xi)) <= tau^-n mu(B_{tau rho}(tau xi)) + C delta^(1/4) |log lambda|.   (11)
6. Reverse inequality (book (12)). Use (7) with phi = 1 on (-inf, rho], phi = 0 on [(1+delta^(1/4)) rho, inf), |phi'| <= 2/(delta^(1/4) rho): h_t = 1 on dB_{tau t} cap B_{tau rho}(tau xi) and h_t = 0 on dB_t minus B_{(1+delta^(1/4))rho}(xi). Integrating over t as in step 5 (the shell contains B_{tau rho}(tau xi) after scaling) gives tau^-n integral_{B_{tau rho}(tau xi)} |grad^M r|^2 <= mu(B_{(1+delta^(1/4))rho}(xi)) + C delta^(1/4)|log lambda|, and tau^-n integral_{B_{tau rho}(tau xi)} r^-2 |x^perp|^2 <= integral_{B_1 minus B_lambda} r^(-n-2)|x^perp|^2 (as r <= tau there and B_{tau rho}(tau xi) is in B_1 minus B_lambda). Hence tau^-n mu(B_{tau rho}(tau xi)) <= mu(B_{(1+delta^(1/4))rho}(xi)) + C delta^(1/4)|log lambda|.   (12)
7. tau = 1: both inequalities are trivial by monotonicity of mu in the radius. With C := max(Lambda + 1, constants above), C = C(n, l, Lambda), the statement holds for all rho in (0, theta] and tau in [2 lambda, 1] (the ENNReal form 'a <= b + c' is (11), (12) with finite quantities).

First variation with homogeneous h and radial C^1 cutoffs, limits taken after averaging
Coarea formula for r = |x| on M
Homogeneous cutoffs h_t with |Dh_t| <= 2/(delta^(1/4) rho |x|)

subproblem.title: Harmonic approximation lemma (Simon 5.3.1)
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1 and eps > 0 there is delta > 0 such that: if B is the open unit ball of R^n, f in L^2(B), g in L^2(B;R^n) with integral_B f grad zeta = - integral_B zeta g for all zeta in C_c^infinity(B), integral_B |g|^2 <= 1, and |integral_B g . grad zeta| <= delta M whenever zeta in C_c^infinity(B) and |grad zeta| <= M everywhere, then there is u harmonic on B (C^2 near each point with Laplacian 0) with integral_B |grad u|^2 <= 1 and integral_B |u - f|^2 <= eps (extended integrals).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 5, Lemma 3.1 and its printed proof (p. 114), a compactness argument; the cited standard facts (Poincare inequality, Rellich compactness, weak compactness, Weyl's lemma) are stated precisely below. Notation: B := open unit ball of R^n, omega_n = L^n(B); 'f in W^{1,2}(B) with weak gradient g' is the contract's IsW12WithGradient f g B (f in L^2(B), g in L^2(B;R^n), integral_B f grad zeta = - integral_B zeta g for zeta in C_c^infinity(B)).

Standard facts used:
(P) Poincare on B [Gilbarg-Trudinger (7.45)]: for f in W^{1,2}(B) with weak gradient g and mean lambda := omega_n^-1 integral_B f: integral_B |f - lambda|^2 <= C_P(n) integral_B |g|^2.
(R) Rellich-Kondrachov [GT Thm 7.26] for the Lipschitz domain B: a sequence bounded in W^{1,2}(B) (L^2 norms of functions and weak gradients bounded) has a subsequence converging in L^2(B).
(W) Bounded sequences in the Hilbert space L^2(B;R^n) have weakly convergent subsequences, and the norm is weakly lower semicontinuous.
(Weyl) If w in L^1_loc(B) satisfies integral_B w Delta zeta = 0 for all zeta in C_c^infinity(B), then w agrees a.e. with a C^infinity function w~ with Delta w~ = 0 on B (proof: w_eps := w * phi_eps (radial mollifier) is smooth and harmonic on B_{1-eps}; harmonic functions satisfy the mean value property, so w_eps * phi_eps' = w_eps and hence w_eps = w_eps' on B_{1 - eps - eps'}; letting eps' -> 0 (Lebesgue points) gives w = w_eps a.e. there).
(U) Weak gradients are unique a.e.; for a C^1 function the classical gradient is a weak gradient.

Proof.
1. Suppose the lemma fails for some n >= 1 and eps > 0. Then for each k >= 1 (taking delta = 1/k) there are f_k, g_k with IsW12WithGradient f_k g_k B, integral_B |g_k|^2 <= 1,
 |integral_B g_k . grad zeta| <= k^-1 M whenever zeta in C_c^infinity(B) and |grad zeta| <= M everywhere,   (1)
 but integral_B |u - f_k|^2 > eps for every u harmonic on B (HarmonicOnNhd) with integral_B |grad u|^2 <= 1.   (2)
2. Let lambda_k := omega_n^-1 integral_B f_k and w_k := f_k - lambda_k; w_k is in W^{1,2}(B) with weak gradient g_k (constants have zero weak gradient since integral_B grad zeta = 0). By (P), integral_B |w_k|^2 <= C_P.
3. By (R) and (W) there is a subsequence k' with w_{k'} -> w in L^2(B) and g_{k'} -> g weakly in L^2(B;R^n). Passing to the limit in integral w_{k'} grad zeta = - integral zeta g_{k'} shows that w is in W^{1,2}(B) with weak gradient g, and integral_B |g|^2 <= liminf integral |g_{k'}|^2 <= 1.
4. For zeta in C_c^infinity(B), M := sup |grad zeta| < infinity and (1) give integral_B g . grad zeta = lim integral_B g_{k'} . grad zeta = 0. Applying the weak-derivative identity to the test functions D_i zeta and summing: integral_B w Delta zeta = - integral_B g . grad zeta = 0. So w is weakly harmonic.
5. By (Weyl), w = w~ a.e. with w~ in C^infinity(B), Delta w~ = 0; by (U), grad w~ = g a.e., so integral_B |grad w~|^2 = integral_B |g|^2 <= 1.
6. u_{k'} := w~ + lambda_{k'} is C^infinity with Laplacian 0 on B, hence HarmonicOnNhd on B; integral_B |grad u_{k'}|^2 <= 1; and integral_B |u_{k'} - f_{k'}|^2 = integral_B |w - w_{k'}|^2 -> 0. For large k' this contradicts (2). Hence for every eps > 0 some delta = delta(n, eps) > 0 works, which is the statement (the energy and L^2 integrals of the contract are the corresponding lintegrals, finite here).
proof_key_steps: Contradiction sequence f_k with delta = 1/k
Poincare inequality for f_k minus its mean
Rellich plus weak compactness give a limit w with weak gradient g and energy <= 1
w is weakly harmonic; Weyl's lemma gives a smooth harmonic representative
w~ + lambda_k converges to f_k in L^2, a contradiction

subproblem.title: Tilt-excess/height estimate (Simon 5.2.1)
subproblem.statement: For every n >= 1 there is C depending only on n such that for every l, open U in R^(n+l), contract rectifiable n-varifold V = v(M,theta) in U with generalized mean curvature H in U, point xi and rho > 0 with closed B_rho(xi) in U, and n-dimensional subspace T: E(xi, rho/2, T) <= C rho^-n integral_{B_rho(xi)} (dist(x - xi, T)/rho)^2 dmu_V + C rho^(2-n) integral_{B_rho(xi)} |H|^2 dmu_V, where E(xi,s,T) = s^-n integral_{B_s(xi)} |p_{T_xM} - p_T|^2 dmu_V (Hilbert-Schmidt norm) and the |H|^2 integral is an extended integral (inequality in [0,inf]).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 5, Lemma 2.1 and its printed proof (pp. 107-108), with the test field taken smooth and integrability made explicit. Notation: mu := V.weight, p_x := V.tangentProj x, T^perp the orthogonal complement of T, x' := p_{T^perp}(x - xi), |.| the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm), ||.|| the operator norm (||A|| <= |A|).

Facts used (cited from the book):
(F1) [Ch. 3, Def. 1.7, Rem. 1.8, Thm. 1.9; contract tangentProj] For mu-a.e. x the approximate tangent space T_xM of M with respect to theta exists, so p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace; x -> p_x is mu-measurable.
(F2) mu(K) < infinity for every compact K in U (structure field integrableOn_mult); mu-a.e. point of U lies in spt V.
(F3) For orthogonal projections P, Q of rank n: trace(P o (I - Q)) = n - trace(PQ) = (1/2)|P - Q|^2.

Proof.
1. Put C := 146 * 2^(n+1) (it depends only on n). Fix l, U, V, H, xi, rho > 0 with B_rho(xi) contained in U (closed ball), and T with dim T = n. subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l, p > n there are beta in (0,1/4] and C, depending only on n,l,p, such that for all L in (0,1], K >= 0, open U, V with generalized mean curvature H, delta, rho with 0 < delta <= (beta L)^(2n+2) and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, and every linear isometry q of R^(n+l) such that dist(x, T_0) <= K delta^(1/(2n+2)) delta rho for all x in spt V cap B_{2 delta rho}(0), where T_0 := q(R^n x {0}), there is f: R^n -> R^l, L-Lipschitz on B^n_{delta rho/2}(0), with |f| <= K delta^(1/(2n+2)) delta rho there and mu_V(B_{delta rho/2}(0) cap (spt V minus q(graph f over B^n_{delta rho/2}))) + H^n(B_{delta rho/2}(0) cap (q(graph f over B^n_{delta rho/2}) minus spt V)) <= C L^-2 integral_{B_{delta rho}(0)} |p_{T_xM} - p_{T_0}|^2 dmu_V.

Source: Simon, Ch. 5, Lemma 2.6 and its printed proof (pp. 110-113), in the contract normalization (arbitrary linear isometry q, T_0 = q(R^n x {0}), height hypothesis with an arbitrary constant K >= 0, documented erratum: the sup bound carries the scale factor sigma_0 = delta rho). Corrections of the printed argument: (i) monotonicity is used with the correct constant Lambda = 4 p delta/(p-n) of Ch. 4, 4.2 (kappa = (p-n)/(4p)); (ii) a dichotomy on the tilt of T_0 (Case A/Case B) makes beta and C independent of K; (iii) pairs of points of G at distance > sigma_0/2 are handled by the height bound (B3); (iv) the loss sqrt(l) in the componentwise extension is absorbed into beta, and a radial retraction gives the exact sup bound; (v) in (9)-(10) the annulus is B_{3s} minus B_s and the ball B_{3s}(zeta) must stay inside B_{3 sigma_0/4}(0), so graph points far from spt V are reached by a continuity (path) argument.

Notation (contract). mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (M = V.carrier, theta = V.mult); spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu; p_x := V.tangentProj x and p_x^perp := I - p_x; |A| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm), ||A|| the operator norm, ||A|| <= |A| <= sqrt(rank A) ||A||; B_s(y) is the closed ball and B^o_s(y) the open ball; omega_n := unitBallVolume n; K(z,s) := (s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) in [0,infinity] (the contract's scaledLpNorm); E(z,s,T) := s^-n integral_{B_s(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu (tiltExcess); kappa := (p-n)/(4p) > 0; a := 1/(2n+2). Under 2.3, if B_s(z) is contained in B_rho(0) then K(z,s)^p = s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p <= (s/rho)^(p-n) rho^(p-n) integral_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p, so K(z,s) <= (s/rho)^(1-n/p) delta <= delta.
Further notation: sigma_0 := delta rho; alpha := a = 1/(2n+2); T_0 := rotatedPlane q; P := p_{T_0}; Q := I - P = p_{T_0^perp}; tilt(A) := integral_A |p_x - P|^2 dmu. Write q^-1 y = graphPoint(a(y), b(y)) with a(y) in R^n, b(y) in R^l; since q is a linear isometry mapping R^n x {0} onto T_0 and {0} x R^l onto T_0^perp, |a(y)| = |Py| <= |y| and |b(y)| = |Qy| = dist(y, T_0).

Sibling used: AffineApproximationLemma, with constant C_A >= 1 (enlarging the sibling's constant preserves both of its inequalities): for 0 < delta <= 1/4, 2.3, xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0), s in (0, 2 delta rho] there is an n-plane T' with C_A^-1 (s^-n integral_{B_{s/2}(xi)} |p_x - p_{T'}|^2)^(1/2) <= s^-1 h(xi,s,T') + K(xi,s) and s^-1 h(xi,s,T') <= C_A delta^alpha, where h(xi,s,T') := sup{dist(x - xi, T') : x in spt V cap B_s(xi)}.

subproblem.title: Lipschitz graph corollary (Simon 5.2.7)
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l, p > n there is beta in (0,1/4] (depending on n,l,p) such that for all L in (0,1], K >= 0, open U, V with generalized mean curvature H, delta, rho with 0 < delta <= (beta L)^(2n+2) and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, every linear isometry q with dist(x, T_0) <= K delta^(1/(2n+2)) delta rho on spt V cap B_{2 delta rho}(0) (T_0 := q(R^n x {0})) and with E(xi, sigma, T_0) <= beta^2 L^2 for all xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho/2}(0), sigma in (0, delta rho/2], there is f: R^n -> R^l, L-Lipschitz on B^n_{delta rho/4}(0), with |f| <= K delta^(1/(2n+2)) delta rho there and spt V cap B_{delta rho/4}(0) = q(graph f over B^n_{delta rho/4}(0)) cap B_{delta rho/4}(0).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 5, Corollary 2.7 and its printed proof (p. 113), which re-uses the set G, the Lipschitz construction and inequality (10) from the proof of Lemma 2.6; those parts are reproduced here (the corollary has its own constant beta). Contract normalization as in 2.6: arbitrary linear isometry q, T_0 = q(R^n x {0}), height constant K >= 0, sup bound K delta^alpha sigma_0. Corrections as in 2.6: monotonicity with the correct constant Lambda = 4 p delta/(p-n) (Ch. 4, 4.2, kappa = (p-n)/(4p)); the annulus in (10) is B_{3s} minus B_s; the extension loss sqrt(l) is absorbed into beta; the sup bound comes from a retraction; graph points far from spt V are reached by a continuity (path) argument.

Notation (contract). mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (M = V.carrier, theta = V.mult); spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu; p_x := V.tangentProj x and p_x^perp := I - p_x; |A| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm), ||A|| the operator norm, ||A|| <= |A| <= sqrt(rank A) ||A||; B_s(y) is the closed ball and B^o_s(y) the open ball; omega_n := unitBallVolume n; K(z,s) := (s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) in [0,infinity] (the contract's scaledLpNorm); E(z,s,T) := s^-n integral_{B_s(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu (tiltExcess); kappa := (p-n)/(4p) > 0; a := 1/(2n+2). Under 2.3, if B_s(z) is contained in B_rho(0) then K(z,s)^p = s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p <= (s/rho)^(p-n) rho^(p-n) integral_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p, so K(z,s) <= (s/rho)^(1-n/p) delta <= delta.
Further notation: sigma_0 := delta rho; alpha := a = 1/(2n+2); T_0 := rotatedPlane q; P := p_{T_0}; Q := I - P; tilt(A) := integral_A |p_x - P|^2 dmu; q^-1 y = graphPoint(a(y), b(y)), so |a(y)| = |Py| <= |y| and |b(y)| = |Qy| = dist(y, T_0); G' := spt V cap B_{sigma_0/2}(0). The tilt hypothesis reads: tilt(B_s(xi)) <= beta^2 L^2 s^n for all xi in G' and s in (0, sigma_0/2].

Sibling used: AffineApproximationLemma, with constant C_A >= 1 (enlarging the constant preserves both inequalities): for 0 < delta <= 1/4, 2.3, xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0), s in (0, 2 delta rho] there is an n-plane T' with C_A^-1 (s^-n integral_{B_{s/2}(xi)} |p_x - p_{T'}|^2)^(1/2) <= s^-1 h(xi,s,T') + K(xi,s) and s^-1 h(xi,s,T') <= C_A delta^alpha, h(xi,s,T') := sup{dist(x - xi, T') : x in spt V cap B_s(xi)}.

Facts used:
(F1) [Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7, Rem. 1.8, Thm. 1.9; contract tangentProj] For mu-a.e. x the approximate tangent space T_xM of M with respect to theta exists; at such x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto the n-dimensional space T_xM, and Theta^n(mu,x) = theta(x) (Rem. 1.8(2)). The map x -> p_x is mu-measurable and bounded (|p_x - p_T|^2 <= 4n), so tilt integrals over compact subsets of U are finite: by Ch. 3, Rem. 1.3 and Rem. 1.8(1), M is covered up to an H^n-null set by countably many H^n-measurable pieces M_j contained in embedded C^1 submanifolds N_j, and for H^n-a.e. x in M_j the space T_xM exists and equals T_xN_j, which depends continuously on x in N_j; since T_xM is unique where theta(x) > 0 (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), p_x agrees mu-a.e. with a Borel map. If Gamma is the graph of a Lipschitz map over (a subset of) an n-plane, then T_xM = T_x Gamma for H^n-a.e. x in M cap Gamma (Rem. 1.8(1)), and T_x Gamma is the range of the differential of the graph map at H^n-a.e. x in Gamma (Rademacher, Ch. 2, 1.4).
(F2) mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0 and mu(R^(n+l) minus U) = 0, so mu-a.e. point lies in spt V; mu(K) < infinity for compact K in U; H^n(M minus spt V) = 0 (because mu(M minus spt V) = 0 and theta > 0 on M); spt V is relatively closed in U; if y in U minus spt V then mu(B^o_r(y)) = 0 for some r > 0.
(M) [Monotonicity: Simon Ch. 4, 4.1-4.10, with the coefficient in front of Lambda in 4.2 equal to kappa = (p-n)/(4p), the value required by the integration after 4.4 (cf. SimonGMT Chapter04 `lpMeanCurvatureKappa`, `LpAnnularCorrection`)]. Let y in R^(n+l) and R > 0 with B_R(y) in U and K(y,R) <= kappa Lambda for some Lambda > 0. (Under 2.3, whenever B_R(y) is contained in B_rho(0) we have K(y,R) <= delta, so Lambda := delta/kappa = 4 p delta/(p-n) is admissible; Lambda <= 1 as soon as delta <= kappa.) Then there are F : (0,R) -> (0,infinity) and numbers G(s,r) such that for all 0 < s <= r < R:

 (M.ii) Phi(r) - Phi(s) = G(s,r) integral_{B_r(y) minus B_s(y)} |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 |x - y|^(-n-2) dmu(x), where Phi(t) := F(t) t^-n mu(B_t(y)) + F(t) - 1 and G(s,r) in [e^-Lambda, e^Lambda].
 (M.iii) Hence Phi is nondecreasing, Theta(y) := lim_{s -> 0} omega_n^-1 s^-n mu(B_s(y)) exists, and omega_n Theta(y) = lim_{s -> 0} Phi(s) <= Phi(r) for every r in (0,R); in particular mu({y}) = 0.

Under 2.3 this applies to W = B^o_rho(0) (H is in L^p(B_rho(0)) since K(0,rho) <= delta < infinity).
 (M.v) If Lambda <= 1 and 0 < s <= r < R, then s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= e^(2 Lambda) r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda. [By (M.ii) Phi(s) <= Phi(r), so F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) = Phi(s) - (F(s) - 1) <= F(r) r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + (F(r) - 1) + Lambda <= e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 Lambda; divide by F(s) >= e^-Lambda.]

Since g_+(0) = g_-(0) = 1 and g_c(0) = 0, there is C_P = C_P(n,p) >= 1 with g_+(t) <= 1 + C_P t, g_-(t) >= 1 - C_P t and g_c(t) <= C_P t on that interval. Put delta_P := min{1/8, kappa, 1/(2 C_P)}.
Claim. If delta <= delta_P, |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2, then (P.i) mu(B_s(y)) <= (1 + C_P delta) omega_n s^n <= 2 omega_n s^n and Theta(y) <= 1 + C_P delta; if moreover y in spt V, then (P.ii) mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - C_P delta) omega_n s^n >= omega_n s^n/2 and (P.iii) integral_{B_s(y)} |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 |x - y|^(-n-2) dmu(x) <= C_P omega_n delta (integrand := 0 at x = y).
Proof. R_y := (1 - 3 delta) rho >= 5 rho/8 > rho/2 >= s, B_{R_y}(y) is contained in B_rho(0) (as |y| + R_y <= rho), so (M) applies at y with R = R_y and Lambda = delta/kappa <= 1, and mu(B_r(y)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n for r < R_y. (P.i): for s <= r < R_y, (M.ii),(M.i) give F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) = Phi(s) - (F(s) - 1) <= Phi(r) + Lambda <= e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 Lambda; dividing by F(s) >= e^-Lambda and letting r -> R_y, omega_n^-1 s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= g_+(delta); Theta(y) is the limit as s -> 0. (P.ii): Theta(y) >= 1 by (M.iv), so by (M.iii) F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n - (F(s) - 1) >= omega_n - Lambda and s^-n mu(B_s(y)) >= e^-Lambda (omega_n - Lambda) = omega_n g_-(delta) (here omega_n - Lambda > 0 because g_-(delta) >= 1/2). (P.iii): for 0 < t < s <= r < R_y, (M.ii),(M.iii) give integral_{B_s(y) minus B_t(y)} |p_x^perp(x-y)|^2 |x-y|^(-n-2) dmu <= e^Lambda (Phi(r) - Phi(t)) <= e^Lambda (e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + Lambda - omega_n Theta(y)) <= e^Lambda (e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + Lambda - omega_n); let r -> R_y and t -> 0 (monotone convergence, mu({y}) = 0) to get <= omega_n g_c(delta).
(Ext) [Ch. 2, 1.2 (McShane), componentwise] An M-Lipschitz map from a subset of R^n to R^l extends to an (sqrt(l) M)-Lipschitz map on R^n.

subproblem.title: Tilt-excess decay theorem (Simon 5.4.5)
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l, p > n there are eta, delta_0 in (0,1/4] depending only on n,l,p such that: if U is open, V has generalized mean curvature H, AllardHypotheses H p delta rho hold with 0 < delta <= delta_0, sigma in (0, delta rho/2], xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0) and T is an n-dimensional subspace, then there is an n-dimensional subspace S with E_*(xi, eta sigma, S) <= eta^(2(1 - n/p)) E_*(xi, sigma, T), where E_*(xi,sigma,T) = max{E(xi,sigma,T), delta^-1 (sigma^(p-n) integral_{B_sigma(xi)} |H|^p dmu_V)^(2/p)} (contract tiltExcessStar).
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 5, Theorem 4.5 and its printed proof (pp. 116-121), which uses 2.1, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1 and 3.4. Corrections of the printed argument: (i) monotonicity is used with the correct constant Lambda = 4 p delta/(p-n) of Ch. 4, 4.2 (kappa = (p-n)/(4p)); (ii) the printed 'we can suppose xi = 0' is made precise by re-centring at xi with the enlarged parameter delta'' = C_1 delta, so that 2.5 and 2.6 apply at centre xi at scale sigma; (iii) consistent radii: 2.6 gives a graph over B^n_{sigma/2}, the harmonic approximation is done on B^n_{sigma/4}, and the final ratio is eta/16; (iv) 'Lip f <= 1' is an operator-norm bound: it gives |D f^j| <= 1 for each component and |Df|^2 <= n (Hilbert-Schmidt), and for the graph Jacobian J_F = sqrt(det(I + Df^T Df)) only 1 <= J_F <= 2^(n/2) and J_F <= 1 + c_n |Df|^2 with c_n := e^(n/2)/2 (not J_F <= 2); these dimension-dependent constants are carried through steps 4-8; (v) printed step (20) uses Remark 2.2, which needs p >= 2; for 1 < p < 2 (which forces n = 1) Lemma A and a one-dimensional sup bound for the height are used instead.

Notation (contract). mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (M = V.carrier, theta = V.mult); spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu; p_x := V.tangentProj x and p_x^perp := I - p_x; |A| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm), ||A|| the operator norm, ||A|| <= |A| <= sqrt(rank A) ||A||; B_s(y) is the closed ball and B^o_s(y) the open ball; omega_n := unitBallVolume n; K(z,s) := (s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) in [0,infinity] (the contract's scaledLpNorm); E(z,s,T) := s^-n integral_{B_s(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu (tiltExcess); kappa := (p-n)/(4p) > 0; a := 1/(2n+2). Under 2.3, if B_s(z) is contained in B_rho(0) then K(z,s)^p = s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p <= (s/rho)^(p-n) rho^(p-n) integral_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p, so K(z,s) <= (s/rho)^(1-n/p) delta <= delta.
Further notation: alpha := 1 - n/p in (0,1); a = 1/(2n+2) (so 2a = 1/(n+1)); E_*(z,s,T) := max{E(z,s,T), delta^-1 K(z,s)^2} with the delta of 2.3 (contract tiltExcessStar; K(z,s) is finite for every ball used below, which lies in B_rho(0)). For an l x n matrix A, J(A) := sqrt(det(I_n + A^T A)), and graph A := {graphPoint(x, A x) : x in R^n}.

Siblings used: TiltExcessHeightEstimate (2.1, constant C_21), AffineApproximationLemma (2.5, constant C_A), LipschitzApproximationLemma (2.6, constants beta_6, C_6; used with L = 1), HarmonicApproximationLemma (3.1). We may and do assume C_21, C_A, C_6 >= 1: enlarging these constants preserves the sibling conclusions, because in each ENNReal inequality the constant multiplies a nonnegative quantity (and in 2.5 enlarging C weakens both inequalities).

Facts used:
(F1) [Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7, Rem. 1.8, Thm. 1.9; contract tangentProj] For mu-a.e. x the approximate tangent space T_xM of M with respect to theta exists; at such x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto the n-dimensional space T_xM, and Theta^n(mu,x) = theta(x) (Rem. 1.8(2)). The map x -> p_x is mu-measurable and bounded (|p_x - p_T|^2 <= 4n), so tilt integrals over compact subsets of U are finite: by Ch. 3, Rem. 1.3 and Rem. 1.8(1), M is covered up to an H^n-null set by countably many H^n-measurable pieces M_j contained in embedded C^1 submanifolds N_j, and for H^n-a.e. x in M_j the space T_xM exists and equals T_xN_j, which depends continuously on x in N_j; since T_xM is unique where theta(x) > 0 (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), p_x agrees mu-a.e. with a Borel map. If Gamma is the graph of a Lipschitz map over (a subset of) an n-plane, then T_xM = T_x Gamma for H^n-a.e. x in M cap Gamma (Rem. 1.8(1)), and T_x Gamma is the range of the differential of the graph map at H^n-a.e. x in Gamma (Rademacher, Ch. 2, 1.4).
(F2) mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0 and mu(R^(n+l) minus U) = 0, so mu-a.e. point lies in spt V; mu(K) < infinity for compact K in U; H^n(M minus spt V) = 0 (because mu(M minus spt V) = 0 and theta > 0 on M); spt V is relatively closed in U; if y in U minus spt V then mu(B^o_r(y)) = 0 for some r > 0.
(M) [Monotonicity: Simon Ch. 4, 4.1-4.10, with the coefficient in front of Lambda in 4.2 equal to kappa = (p-n)/(4p), the value required by the integration after 4.4 (cf. SimonGMT Chapter04 `lpMeanCurvatureKappa`, `LpAnnularCorrection`)]. Let y in R^(n+l) and R > 0 with B_R(y) in U and K(y,R) <= kappa Lambda for some Lambda > 0. Then there are F : (0,R) -> (0,infinity) and numbers G(s,r) such that for all 0 < s <= r < R:
 (M.i) e^-Lambda <= F(r) <= e^Lambda and |F(r) - 1| <= (1/2) e^(Lambda/2) Lambda (r/R)^(1-n/p); if Lambda <= 1, then |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda (r/R)^(1-n/p) <= Lambda; F(r) -> 1 as r -> 0.

Under 2.3 this applies to W = B^o_rho(0) (H is in L^p(B_rho(0)) since K(0,rho) <= delta < infinity).
 (M.v) If Lambda <= 1 and 0 < s <= r < R, then s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= e^(2 Lambda) r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 e^Lambda Lambda. [By (M.ii) Phi(s) <= Phi(r), so F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) = Phi(s) - (F(s) - 1) <= F(r) r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + (F(r) - 1) + Lambda <= e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 Lambda; divide by F(s) >= e^-Lambda.]
(P) [2.4 of the text, with explicit constants]. Assume 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho) with delta <= min{1/8, kappa}, so Lambda := delta/kappa <= 1. Consider the smooth functions of t in [0, min{1/8, kappa}] (with Lambda_t := t/kappa)

Since g_+(0) = g_-(0) = 1 and g_c(0) = 0, there is C_P = C_P(n,p) >= 1 with g_+(t) <= 1 + C_P t, g_-(t) >= 1 - C_P t and g_c(t) <= C_P t on that interval. Put delta_P := min{1/8, kappa, 1/(2 C_P)}.
Claim. If delta <= delta_P, |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2, then (P.i) mu(B_s(y)) <= (1 + C_P delta) omega_n s^n <= 2 omega_n s^n and Theta(y) <= 1 + C_P delta; if moreover y in spt V, then (P.ii) mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - C_P delta) omega_n s^n >= omega_n s^n/2 and (P.iii) integral_{B_s(y)} |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 |x - y|^(-n-2) dmu(x) <= C_P omega_n delta (integrand := 0 at x = y).
Proof. (P.i): for s <= r < R_y, (M.ii),(M.i) give F(s) s^-n mu(B_s(y)) = Phi(s) - (F(s) - 1) <= Phi(r) + Lambda <= e^Lambda r^-n mu(B_r(y)) + 2 Lambda; dividing by F(s) >= e^-Lambda and letting r -> R_y, omega_n^-1 s^-n mu(B_s(y)) <= g_+(delta); Theta(y) is the limit as s -> 0. subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l, p > n there are delta_0, gamma in (0,1) and C, depending only on n,l,p, such that for every open U, V with generalized mean curvature H, 0 < delta <= delta_0 and rho with AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, AllardConclusion V p delta rho gamma C holds: there are a linear isometry q of R^(n+l) and u: R^n -> R^l, C^1 on the closed ball B^n_{gamma rho}(0), with u(0) = 0, Du(0) = 0 (derivative within the ball), spt V cap B_{gamma rho}(0) = q(graph u over B^n_{gamma rho}(0)) cap B_{gamma rho}(0), and rho^-1 sup|u| + sup|Du| + rho^(1-n/p) sup_{x != y} |x - y|^-(1-n/p) |Du(x) - Du(y)| <= C delta^(1/(2n+2)) (suprema over the closed ball, Hilbert-Schmidt norms, in [0,inf]).

The printed proof fixes delta = delta(n,l,p) and takes gamma = delta/4; as the contract README notes, the rate C delta^(1/(2n+2)) at a gamma independent of delta needs more. This is supplied in Part III (not in the printed text): the conical excess at 0, which is O(delta) by monotonicity, bounds the height of the already established graph over a fixed fraction of B_rho(0) by radial integration; then Lemma A and the decay iteration give the rate.

subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l, p > n and every gamma in (0,1) there are delta_0 in (0,1) and C, depending on gamma,n,l,p, such that for every open U, V with generalized mean curvature H, 0 < delta <= delta_0 and rho with AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, AllardConclusion V p delta rho gamma C holds (the conclusion of Theorem 5.2 on the ball of radius gamma rho, with constant C).

The proof below follows the announced route: 6.1 and monotonicity give mass-ratio pinching at every point of spt V cap B_{gamma_b rho}(0); Theorem 5.2 then gives local graphs at a fixed scale; 6.1 again forces spt V into a thin cone around the tangent plane T_0 at 0, so the local graphs patch to one graph over T_0; the rate comes from the conical excess at 0 (O(delta) by monotonicity), radial integration, Lemma A and the decay iteration of 4.5. subproblem.title: Regular set is open and dense (Simon 5.7.3)
subproblem.statement: If n >= 1, U is open, V = v(M,theta) has generalized mean curvature H in U with H locally in L^p(mu_V), p > n, and theta is a positive integer for mu_V-a.e. x in spt V, then there is an open O with reg V = O cap spt V, and spt V = closure(reg V) cap U, where reg V is the set of xi in spt V such that open B_rho(xi) cap spt V is an n-dimensional C^1 submanifold (IsC1Submanifold n) for some rho > 0.

Source: Simon, Ch. 5, Definition 7.2 and Corollary 7.3 with its printed proof (p. 128-129): openness of reg V in spt V is immediate from 7.2, and density follows by normalizing the multiplicity by the least integer density N in a ball and applying 7.1 at a point of density 1. Notation: mu = V.weight, spt V = V.support = U cap spt mu (relatively closed in U), reg V = V.regularSet.

Sibling used: AllardRegularityTheorem (5.2: delta_7, gamma_7). Proof.
1. Since mu-a.e. point lies in spt V (F2), the hypothesis gives theta in {1, 2, ...} mu-a.e.; in particular theta >= 1 a.e., and with H in L^p_loc, Theta >= 1 on spt V (M).
